rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Sulphur dioxide is the two-faced gas. Prepared from **Na₂SO₃ + dil. H₂SO₄** (or burning S, or roasting FeS₂), it is an angular, pungent, water-soluble oxide that gives the **weak dibasic H₂SO₃**. Sitting at S(+4), it reduces upward — decolourising **KMnO₄**, converting **I₂ to HI**, lifting Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺ — and oxidises downward — the **sulphur fog** of 2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O, and continued Mg burning in the gas.…

rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Two-Faced Gas SO₂: reducing and oxidising, acidic, bleaching (temporarily), preservative, refrigerant. Its dual redox personality and bleaching contrast with Cl₂ are the exam heart.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Preparation - Lab: **Na₂SO₃ + dil. H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + SO₂ + H₂O** (or NaHSO₃ + HCl). - From sulphur: **S + O₂ → SO₂** (burning); from sulphides: **4FeS₂ + 11O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃ + 8SO₂** (roasting, industrial); **Cu + 2H₂SO₄(conc) → CuSO₄ + SO₂ + 2H₂O**; **Cu + dil. HNO₃** route also gives NO — avoid confusion. - Collected by **upward delivery** (heavier than air, 2.27 g/L).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Reducer: KMnO4 decolourised, I2 -> HI, Fe3+ -> Fe2+. Oxidiser: 2H2S + SO2 -> 3S + 2H2O. Bleach = reduction = temporary vs Cl2 oxidation = permanent. Prep: Na2SO3 + dil H2SO4. E220 preservative.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Sulphur at +4 is a middle child: it can climb to +6 (reducing KMnO4, I2, Fe3+) or sink to 0 or -2 (oxidising H2S, Mg, CO) - SO2's dual redox personality is the oxidation-state ladder in action.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: SO2 prep: Na2SO3 + dil H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + SO2 + H2O; S + O2; 4FeS2 + 11O2 -> 2Fe2O3 + 8SO2 (roasting); Cu + 2H2SO4(conc). Angular molecule (~119 deg, sp2, one lone pair), pungent, heavier than air (upward delivery). ACIDIC: SO2 + H2O <=> H2SO3 (weak dibasic); 2NaOH + SO2 -> Na2SO3.…

rows.text: Dried apricots stay bright orange because sulphur dioxide (E220) stops enzymatic browning - food chemistry on the supermarket shelf.

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why SO₂ is both reducer and oxidiser - S sits at +4, the middle of its range (−2 to +6): it can climb to +6 (reducing behaviour with KMnO₄, I₂, Fe³⁺) or sink to 0/−2 (oxidising behaviour with H₂S, Mg, CO). The H₂S reaction shows both faces in one flask — SO₂ oxidises H₂S while any excess SO₂ in water would reduce permanganate.…  ·  ## 5. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Compare the bleaching action of SO2 and Cl2.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions - **"SO₂ bleaches like Cl₂."** Opposite mechanisms and permanence — quote both equations. - **"SO₂ is a strong acid anhydride."** It gives the *weak* H₂SO₃; SO₃ gives strong H₂SO₄. - **"SO₂ is always a reducer."** With H₂S and Mg it is the oxidiser — the +4 middle state cuts both ways.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application - Two reduction equations (KMnO₄, I₂) + one oxidation equation (H₂S) = the dual-personality answer. - The bleaching contrast table (mechanism, permanence) is a 3-mark staple. - Food preservation (E220) is the modern-use mark.
